records.title: SQLite FTS5 documentation: build, tokenizers, content modes, triggers, repair, snippets
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite documentation inspected 2026-10-10; no versioned URL. Investigator's S06 records the 3.53.4 upstream source snapshot, not the app deployment.
records.locator: Sections 2.1, 3 and 3.1, 4.3.1, 4.4.1-4.4.4, 5.1.3, 6.7, 6.12; especially FTS5 build options, unicode61, contentless-delete, external-content trigger examples, REPLACE limitation on the FTS virtual table, rank=1 integrity-check, and rebuild.
records.observed_operation: Opened and inspected current page sections on build activation, query strings, tokenization, contentless/contentless-delete/external-content table semantics, trigger-based consistency, backfill gaps, integrity-check, rebuild, and snippet limits.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 source-tree configure currently requires --enable-fts5 while amalgamation defaults differ and may change. Ordinary contentless tables reject SQL UPDATE/DELETE and return NULL for columns other than rowid; contentless-delete is documented as available since 3.43.0 and permits DELETE, INSERT OR REPLACE, and UPDATE only when all user-defined columns receive values, but not the FTS delete command. External-content tables fetch values from a named same-database content table; consistency remains the application’s responsibility, trigger creation does not index old rows, rank=1 is needed for external-content comparison, and rebuild uses the content table. The FTS5 page says new code should prefer contentless-delete over ordinary contentless; this is not a universal preference over external-content.
records.applicability: Supports conditional FTS5 design claims and correct distinctions among three table modes only. Actual app library, configuration, table schema, and writes are unverified; the current live page is not a deployment-version pin.

records.title: SQLite 3.43.0 release record
records.locator: Release item 1, lines 20-21; source ID lines 38-41.
records.observed_operation: Checked the released version history for introduction of contentless-delete FTS5 indexes.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The release record establishes that this mode shipped in SQLite 3.43.0; it does not prove the application embeds or enables a SQLite build at or above that version.
records.applicability: Version-gates the correction to the user’s contentless assumption. Deployment applicability remains UNKNOWN until each target runtime is probed.

records.title: SQLite ON CONFLICT REPLACE semantics
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite documentation; page reports last updated 2025-11-22 13:15:11Z; no versioned release URL.
records.observed_operation: Checked behavior of INSERT OR REPLACE when a unique or primary-key conflict deletes a pre-existing row before inserting the replacement.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite documents that delete triggers caused by REPLACE fire if and only if recursive triggers are enabled. This is specific to rows deleted by the REPLACE conflict strategy; it does not describe ordinary UPDATE or DELETE statements.
records.applicability: Applies to the proposed canonical-note trigger design only if the actual note write path uses REPLACE. No such app operation was observed.

records.title: SQLite recursive_triggers pragma
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite pragma documentation inspected 2026-10-10; the page says recursive-trigger support arrived in 3.6.18 and was initially OFF for compatibility, and says the default may change.
records.observed_operation: Checked the connection-scoped setting that governs whether REPLACE-induced deletes fire delete triggers.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The pragma can be queried or set on a database connection. Historical default was OFF; SQLite permits a future default change, so a design must inspect/configure the exact runtime instead of relying on an assumed default.
records.applicability: Makes the REPLACE trigger caveat testable on each shipped connection; does not establish the application setting.

records.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexWriter
records.locator: commit, delete_term, commit_opstamp, and add_document methods, lines 178-213.
records.observed_operation: Read index add/delete/commit visibility and recovery-point contracts relevant to an outbox-driven sidecar.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Commit blocks and publishes/persists additions since the previous commit; recovery resumes from the last successful commit opstamp. Deletes affect previously committed and earlier same-commit documents and are visible only after commit. The documentation describes index operations, not automatic tracking of external SQLite relations.
records.applicability: Supports the sidecar’s need for explicit change capture, ordering, commit acknowledgement, and replay. Collection membership propagation remains application-owned.

records.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexReader
records.observed_operation: Checked search visibility after commit and reader/searcher refresh policy.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: OnCommitWithDelay is the default, usually reflects a commit rapidly, but may take tens of milliseconds; explicit reload can force deterministic state in tests.
records.applicability: Supports an explicit Tantivy freshness barrier; runtime behavior still requires testing in the selected application.

records.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 tokenizer documentation
records.locator: default tokenizer lines 59-69; custom pipeline lines 74-86; AsciiFoldingFilter lines 125-126; RemoveLongFilter description lines 143-148.
records.observed_operation: Inspected the implicit default tokenizer, SimpleTokenizer, RemoveLongFilter, LowerCaser, punctuation splitting, and explicit AsciiFoldingFilter behavior.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The default splits punctuation/whitespace, lowercases, and drops tokens over 40 characters; RemoveLongFilter documents limits in UTF-8 bytes. The code example orders RemoveLongFilter before LowerCaser. ASCII folding is an explicit filter and maps only characters with ASCII equivalents.
records.applicability: Supports the draft’s explicit analyzer direction while underscoring that folding and byte/character limits must be pinned and tested; it does not establish parity with FTS5.

records.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 TopDocs
records.observed_operation: Checked score direction and deterministic equal-score tie key.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: order_by_score sorts by decreasing BM25; equal sort keys use ascending internal DocAddress.
records.applicability: Confirms the draft’s canonical-note-ID tie-break requirement; internal address is not public note identity.

records.title: Tantivy issue 3031: malformed query panic report
records.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-08-05; observed open on 2026-10-10. Reporter identifies Tantivy 0.22.1 and tantivy-query-grammar 0.22.0. Linked commit 28b2ed185381b59c17530bb37cb9e481921ac1f2 is in a contributor fork, not an upstream release.
records.locator: Issue report/version/input lines 130-172; reproduction and outcomes lines 185-222; activity and linked commit lines 225-236.
records.observed_operation: Inspected upstream issue status, reported input '- *', stated dependency versions, and provenance of the linked fix-like change.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The report is bounded to the stated old versions and specific malformed inputs. Neither the fork commit nor the issue page establishes that Tantivy 0.26.2 is affected or fixed.
records.applicability: Supports retaining exact-version malformed-query tests. Current pinned-release outcome is honestly unresolved.

records.title: SQLite write-ahead log documentation
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite documentation inspected 2026-10-10; no versioned URL.
records.locator: Overview and WAL operation/checkpoint sections, lines 61-99.
records.observed_operation: Checked WAL commit record semantics, same-host shared memory, multiple-database atomicity limit, companion files, and default 1000-page auto-checkpoint.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL is opt-in; its commit record is appended to the WAL, it relies on shared memory and does not work over a network filesystem, transactions across attached databases are not atomic as a set, and the auto-checkpoint threshold is a configurable default.
records.applicability: Supports the draft’s local-store/WAL caveats and separation of SQLite transaction guarantees from dual-store Tantivy writes. App journal mode is unknown.

records.title: SQLite transactional behavior
records.released_version_or_commit: Live upstream SQLite documentation inspected 2026-10-10; no versioned URL.
records.observed_operation: Checked SQLite’s single-transaction crash/power-loss atomicity statement.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The source describes changes inside one SQLite transaction; it does not make one SQLite transaction atomic with changes to an external Tantivy directory. Journal mode, VFS, and storage conditions remain relevant and are covered by the SQLite journal documentation.
records.applicability: Supports co-transactional canonical note plus FTS trigger mutations when both are in one SQLite database transaction only.

reviewed_source_conflicts.observation: The 3.43.0 release record introduced contentless-delete. Current FTS5 docs say to prefer that mode over ordinary contentless, while separately documenting external-content tables with source-table lookup, triggers, integrity-check, and rebuild.
reviewed_source_conflicts.resolution: These statements do not conflict with the draft’s conditional external-content preference. The recommendation compares contentless-delete to ordinary contentless, not to external content; source-table retrieval and content-based rebuild are material distinctions for this adapter.

reviewed_source_conflicts.observation: Upstream issue 3031 remains open for the reported 0.22.1 / grammar 0.22.0 panic, while a fix-like commit is linked from a contributor fork. Tantivy 0.26.2 package metadata in inherited S07 identifies a newer grammar dependency range but does not prove release behavior for the reported input.
reviewed_source_conflicts.resolution: Do not infer either persistence or fix in 0.26.2. Preserve exact-version testing and use a bounded typed query interface.
